usageNotes: Use this to update host-level firewall settings (enable/disable, log levels, conntrack tuning, synflood protection) on a specific PVE node managed through PDM. The caller must hold Resource.Modify on the remote; supply the digest returned by the corresponding GET to prevent overwriting concurrent changes. Returns null synchronously — there is no UPID; the change takes effect immediately on the target node.

examples.summary: Enable the node firewall with synflood protection and warning-level inbound logging

tips: Always fetch the current options first (GET firewall/options) and pass the returned digest to guard against concurrent edits.
Setting enable=false disables ALL host firewall rules on that node — existing VM/CT rules are unaffected but the node itself becomes unprotected.
nftables is a tech-preview feature; do not enable it on production nodes unless you have tested compatibility with your PVE version.
Use the delete array to revert individual settings to their defaults rather than explicitly setting them — this avoids stale values persisting in the config file.
nf_conntrack_max default (262144) can be exhausted on busy hypervisors with many VMs; raise it before seeing 'table full' kernel warnings.
nf_conntrack_helpers should only list protocols actually in use; enabling unnecessary helpers (e.g., sip, pptp) widens the attack surface.
